parts.note: not pop or punk for teenagers: the music sung while a baby's bed is rocked to and fro

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock music' reads as the genre; it is the gentle rocking of a baby's bed, and the song sung over it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lullaby sung to soothe an infant to sleep in its rocking bed is literally music for the very young.

parts.note: a cab is a car hired with its driver, a taxi

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An explorer takes a taxi and climbs in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' turns TO into OT, which in a down entry reads upwards beneath CAB. John Cabot was the Venetian-born navigator who reached North America for England in 1497.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cabot was a fifteenth-century navigator who sailed for England, a famous voyager of discovery.

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left, it rained'
certain means definite, sure

explanation.surface: Only confirm something once it is definite.
explanation.definitionFit: To make sure of a fact by checking is to establish or verify it.

clue.text: Commons not the habitat of such flowers

definitions.text: Commons not the habitat of such flowers

parts.words: Commons not the habitat of such flowers
parts.note: commons look like open grassland where wild flowers grow, but the House of Commons is not where peers and their wives sit: they belong in the Lords

explanation.walkthrough: Commons reads as common land; it is the House of Commons, where the nobility do not sit. The answer is also a name for the wild arum, or cuckoo pint, a British woodland plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a folk name for wild arum, and peers and peeresses are not members of the elected lower chamber of Parliament.

parts.note: not a dull person, but a person not singled out or named at all, an unspecified individual

explanation.walkthrough: 'Undistinguished' suggests mediocre; here it means not identified, any person you cannot single out.
explanation.definitionFit: An unnamed, unidentified person, any individual at all, is literally a character nobody distinguishes.

clue.text: Unsettled CID man upset about nothing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the next piece
upset means overturned or knocked about, so the letters of CID and man are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A rattled detective from the CID is upset over nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles the detective and his colleague together, and 'about' wraps the result round a zero; the surface's flustered policeman hides a wandering people.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandering peoples with no fixed home live an unsettled, roving life.

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the word is read in the return direction, backwards

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, and the 's gives PETS

explanation.walkthrough: 'come-back' turns PETS (a favourite's) into STEP; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a stage in a process, one phase or degree of progress.

parts.note: topping sounds like old-fashioned slang for excellent, but it means worn on top, on the head

explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' reads as the dated British slang for splendid; here it means sitting on top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled crescent worn on the head is an ornament literally placed on top.

clue.text: The claimant's quiet about an offer

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

a tender is an offer, as in a bid for a contract

explanation.surface: A claimant is quietly discussing an offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The claimant' reads as a party in a lawsuit; the answer is a claimant to a throne, like the Old Pretender to the British crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender is a person who lays claim to a title or throne, especially without a just right.

clue.text: A star ashamed at performing badly — how crazy

indicators.note: doing a poor job of performing suggests the letters are put through a botched routine, rearranged

explanation.surface: A star is ashamed of a poor performance and asks how crazy it was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing badly' rearranges the fourteen letters of A STAR ASHAMED AT. The phrase recalls the Hatter in Alice in Wonderland, mad from mercury used in making hats.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom compares someone to a famously deranged hatmaker, meaning utterly insane.

clue.text: This may well be used to bind animals

definitions.text: This may well be used to bind

parts.note: a buck is a male deer or rabbit
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Rope like this might be used to tie up livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'animals', supplies two creatures side by side. Bind is meant as bookbinding: the answer is a stiff cloth used to cover books.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a stiffened coarse cloth used in bookbinding to cover boards.

clue.text: A university man's shrewd where there's friction

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a university graduate
the 's of man's supplies an S
sage means wise, shrewd

explanation.surface: A clever graduate is wise to where the trouble lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'friction' suggests conflict, but it is rubbing: the definition is a rubdown.
explanation.definitionFit: A massage is a kneading and rubbing of the body, so friction is its whole technique.

clue.text: A carry-over for the new matron

definitions.text: A carry-over for the new matron

parts.words: A carry-over for the new matron
parts.note: carry-over sounds like a balance brought forward; it is the doorway a groom carries his bride across, matron meaning a married woman

explanation.walkthrough: 'matron' suggests a hospital, but it is an old word for a married woman; by custom a groom lifts his new wife over the doorstep.
explanation.definitionFit: The doorstep of a home is where, by tradition, a husband carries his bride across.

clue.text: Saw a large number ahead of time

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, a large number
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone saw a large crowd ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the verb; it is the noun for an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional proverb or maxim, a saying repeated down the years.
A railway service of linked carriages is a form of transport; to train is to school or coach someone.

parts.note: taken as written
to tame is to subdue, bring under control
NT is the National Trust, the British charity that preserves historic buildings and countryside

explanation.surface: Will a setback crush the conservationists?
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-back' reverses SET to TES. NT is Britain's National Trust, which preserves historic houses and landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is a will, the legal document disposing of property after death.

parts.note: ex means former, late, as in an ex-wife
claimed means demanded as a right

explanation.surface: Someone telephoned late and made demands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' reads as after hours; it means former, EX.
explanation.definitionFit: To call out suddenly, as in surprise or protest, is to cry out loudly.

parts.note: not flattered or glamorised, but literally made bigger to the eye, as through a lens

explanation.walkthrough: 'great' reads as splendid; it means large, as when a lens enlarges something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seen through a lens appears enlarged, so it has been made to look bigger.

clue.text: An individual T-shirt with no back

parts.note: a singlet is a sleeveless vest, a kind of T-shirt

indicators.note: back means turned backwards, so the word no is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wears a unique T-shirt with nothing printed on the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the little negative round; 'with' is only a link. 'T-shirt' suggests a print, but the garment is a sleeveless vest.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is a person or thing on its own, a lone one rather than part of a pair.

indicators.note: represented means shown in another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Trees are depicted in a mosaic picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges TREES AS into TESSERA. The definition is generous: a tessera is a single tile in a mosaic, with 'in' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one small square of stone or glass from which a mosaic is assembled.

clue.text: Clear of all charges, the Parisian is irritating

parts.note: nett means after deductions, free of all charges
les is French for the (plural), as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: Acquitted of every charge, the Frenchman is still annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear of all charges' sounds like acquittal; it is the nett sum after deductions.
explanation.definitionFit: Nettles as a verb means annoys or provokes, like the sting of the plant.

indicators.note: some of means only part of the word strangers is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Some strangers cause offence.
explanation.definitionFit: To anger someone is to provoke or offend them, causing displeasure.

clue.text: Before midday the aim is better

parts.note: am, ante meridiem, means before noon
an end is an aim, a goal

explanation.surface: In the morning the aim is to improve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is a verb here, to improve; 'the' and 'is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend something is to improve or correct it.

parts.note: E is east, a compass direction

to can mean on, as in 'put the lid to'

taken as written

parts.note: late means advanced, as in late in the day

explanation.definitionFit: A lattice window has small panes set in a criss-cross framework of lead strips.

clue.text: Do secretarial work of a sort

explanation.definitionFit: Keyboarding letters is typing; a type is also a kind or sort.

explanation.definitionFit: This children's pastime involves making shapes with a loop of string passed between the fingers.
